name: HivePunk 632
subject: Uniswap/v4-periphery
thesis: This is a widely forked extension layer for Uniswap v4 rather than a proven, actively shipped product. The combination of high fork count with in-development language and zero real-work commits in the last 30 days suggests interest exceeds demonstrated recent shipping.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Uniswap/v4-periphery has 1 raw commits in the last 30 days, 0 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: UNKNOWN

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: v4-periphery hosts logic built on top of Uniswap v4 core pool logic, including hook contracts and position managers.
claims.quote: v4-periphery hosts the logic that builds on top of the core pool logic like hook contracts, position managers, and even possibly libraries needed for integrations.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Uniswap v4 is described as a new automated market maker protocol providing extensibility and customizability to pools.

risks: README says contracts are still in development and further periphery contracts have not yet been built, so production readiness is uncertain.
Recent activity check found 0 real-work commits in the last 30 days, suggesting maintenance pace may be low or focused on review and documentation.
Open issues list router, quoter, position-manager, descriptor and notifier fixes related to DoS, slippage bypass, overflow and griefing risks.
Forks are not evidence of production use, and no deployment, TVL, volume or user activity figures were shown in the pages read.
Hook contracts are customizable by design, so individual hooks may carry risks not present in the core pool logic.
